Cape May, NJ: Where The Beach, Bungalows, And Bliss Converge

This article was collaboratively written by Tara Falkenberg + Buzzy, our creative AI assistant.

If I were to pick one underrated travel spot that deserves all the hype in the world, it would be Cape May. Now, I know what you're thinking - "Cape May? What is that, some kind of mayonnaise brand?" But trust me, this little town tucked away in New Jersey is a gem worth visiting. Here are just a few reasons why:

House on the Beach?

I mean, come on, who doesn't love a beachfront bungalow? Cape May has some of the most charming beach homes, complete with wrap-around porches and picturesque views of the ocean. My family and I rented a house for a week, and let me tell you, there's nothing quite like waking up to the sound of waves crashing outside your window.

Drive-to Destination

One of the biggest appeals of Cape May is that it's a drive-to destination for people on the northeast corridor. No need to worry about flights or layovers, just hop in the car and go. Plus, the drive down the New Jersey coast is quite lovely - you'll pass through quaint towns and scenic routes.

Casual Nature

Cape May is a place where you can be yourself. It's not overrun by tourists or filled with pretentious people. It's chill, laid back, and you'll love that vibe. You can wear your flip-flops and sundress (or board shorts and a tank top, no judgment here) as you sip your favorite brew at the local pub.

Bird Watching

Cape May is actually a world-renowned birdwatching spot. No, I'm not trying to be funny. It's genuinely a fantastic place to sit back and watch the most amazing bird species migrate. It's perfect for budding ornithologists, bird enthusiasts, or even if you're just like "eh" about birds. I promise you; this experience will make your heart sing.

The Food

Oh, come on, I couldn't make this list and not talk about food, right? Cape May has a glorious array of delightful seafood and homely eateries. Treat yourself to some mouth-watering New Jersey lobster or snack on some freshly made nachos – it's all here for you, my friend.

So next time you're looking for a beach getaway, skip the crowded tourist destinations and head to Cape May. You won't regret it.
